profiles.meeting_scenario: An internal coordination meeting at a mid-sized asset manager preparing a six-week pilot for an LLM-assisted equity signal stack inspired by recent survey findings on financial prediction and trading. The Quant Research workstream is packaging candidate signals from earnings calls, filings, and news into a research evidence pack, while the ML Platform and Data Ops workstream is wiring the ingestion, retrieval, scoring, and daily publishing pipeline into the firm's research environment. The meeting happens ten days before a CIO and portfolio-manager checkpoint. Agenda: confirm what will be delivered for the checkpoint, align on the signal feed interface and daily publishing cadence, check which benchmark materials both teams are using, and clarify handoffs around the covered equity universe. Expected outcome: both participants leave believing they have aligned on timeline, artifacts, and responsibilities for the pilot checkpoint.

members.name: Sofia Chen
members.expertise: Equity signal research, NLP for financial documents, portfolio construction under turnover and capacity constraints
members.background: Former buy-side quant researcher who now leads the firm's alternative data and language-model research pod for US equities.
members.private_state: She wants the checkpoint to establish that the LLM signal is investment-grade, not just technically feasible, because the CIO is skeptical of flashy demos without time-safe evaluation and realistic trading assumptions.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the signal will have a 'daily refresh,' they mean it will be available before the market opens so PMs can trade on it that same day.
Something is only 'ready for PM review' if the research packet includes leakage checks, cost-adjusted performance, and capacity commentary rather than just a functioning feed.
The shared 'benchmark pack' is the Monday email appendix v3 from the steering committee, because that is the latest document she has been using to shape evaluation expectations.
Unless someone states otherwise, 'US coverage' means the team's standard top-1000 liquid US common-stock universe with ADRs and duplicate share classes excluded.

members.name: Daniel Ruiz
members.role: ML Platform & Market Data Operations Manager
members.expertise: Production data pipelines, vendor entitlement management, orchestration, model-serving interfaces, audit logging
members.background: Former fintech data engineering lead who now runs the firm's platform layer connecting market data, text feeds, and research applications.
members.private_state: He wants the checkpoint to demonstrate that the pipeline is stable, auditable, and within current vendor and infrastructure constraints, so his team is not forced into last-minute architecture changes.
hidden_assumptions: A 'daily refresh' means one completed batch per trading day using the prior day's finalized text and market data, which is sufficient for research consumers.
Something is 'ready for PM review' once the feed lands reliably in the research environment with metadata, lineage, and a dashboard showing recent outputs.
The operative 'benchmark pack' is the Jira-linked Confluence spec frozen two weeks ago, because platform teams should build against the ticketed reference, not informal email attachments.
Unless clarified, 'US coverage' means every US-listed symbol for which the firm has both price history and licensed English text, including ADRs if the vendor classifies them as US.
If research wants a narrower live universe, that filtering should happen downstream in the research layer rather than in the platform publishing job.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that the pilot feed will have a 'daily refresh' before the checkpoint.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Sofia means a pre-market refresh by about 7:00 AM ET that includes overnight filings, earnings-call transcripts, and news so the signal can inform same-day trading decisions.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel means one completed overnight batch per trading day based on prior-day finalized inputs, typically publishing after the close or late evening for next-day research access.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In coordination meetings, 'daily refresh' sounds like a standard cadence term, so both hear confirmation of frequency and do not think to unpack the exact cut-off time or trading-day usability.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as 'ready for PM review'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say they want the package 'ready for PM review' by next week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Sofia means the signal has passed research-grade checks: time-safe evaluation, leakage review, cost and turnover overlays, and at least a stable evidence summary on the top-1000 liquid universe.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel means the operational workflow is stable enough for PMs to inspect outputs: the pipeline runs automatically, data lineage is visible, and the dashboard shows recent signal values and explanations.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds like a simple milestone everyone would share, but each function naturally applies its own completion standard—research validity versus operational readiness—without realizing the other is using a different bar.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to aligning with 'the benchmark pack' already circulated for the checkpoint.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Sofia is thinking of the Monday email appendix v3 that added capacity notes, latency reporting, and a stricter time-safe evaluation checklist.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel is thinking of the older Confluence page linked in Jira, labeled benchmark pack v2, which omits the new capacity tab and still frames latency at a coarser batch level.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both documents share nearly the same title and were discussed in overlapping channels, so each person assumes the other is referencing the same artifact and sees no need to restate the version.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the pilot should show 'US coverage' for the checkpoint.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Sofia means the firm's research-standard top-1000 liquid US common-stock universe, excluding ADRs, ETFs, and duplicate share classes, because that is the universe used in her backtests.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel means all US-listed symbols with both price data and licensed English text coverage—around 1,800 names—including ADRs when the vendor tags them as US.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both use the same high-level label because the universe choice feels like established house shorthand, yet each function inherited a different default boundary from its own workflows.

For me, ready for PM review means the packet has time-safe evaluation, leakage checks, costs, turnover, and at least some capacity commentary on the standard top-1000 liquid US universe. If Daniel says we're on track, I want to make sure the platform handoff supports that bar without having to relitigate basics in front of the CIO.

turns.utterance: Perfect. Then from my side I want the PM review materials to show realistic costs, capacity, and leakage checks alongside a few signal examples, so the package feels properly ready for PM review rather than just technically interesting.

As long as that’s understood, I’m comfortable committing. I don’t want the meeting to morph into a request for new infra work in the last week.

And the daily refresh timestamps need to support the same-day trading examples in my deck; otherwise I’ll have to explain away avoidable confusion in front of PMs. I’m sure we mean the same thing there.
